alerts.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued March 10 at 2:44PM CDT until March 11 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
alerts.description:
...ELEVATED TO CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER RISK EXPECTED ON WEDNESDAY...

.A precipitous drop off in relative humidity (RH) values are
expected to take place Wednesday afternoon following the passage
of a dryline. The combination of low RH values ranging between
15-30%, an ongoing drought ranging from D2 (Severe Drought) to D4
(Exceptional Drought), and breezy northwest winds will result in
elevated to critical fire weather risk on Wednesday across all of
Deep South Texas, excluding the island.

The National Weather Service in Brownsville has issued a Fire
Weather Watch for breezy winds and low relative humidity, which
is in effect from Wednesday afternoon through Wednesday evening.

* WINDS...10-20 mph gusting as high as 25-30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 15-30 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Mid to upper 90s.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread quickly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.

alerts.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued March 10 at 2:44PM CDT until March 11 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
alerts.description:
...ELEVATED TO CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER RISK EXPECTED ON WEDNESDAY...

.A precipitous drop off in relative humidity (RH) values are
expected to take place Wednesday afternoon following the passage
of a dryline. The combination of low RH values ranging between
15-30%, an ongoing drought ranging from D2 (Severe Drought) to D4
(Exceptional Drought), and breezy northwest winds will result in
elevated to critical fire weather risk on Wednesday across all of
Deep South Texas, excluding the island.

The National Weather Service in Brownsville has issued a Fire
Weather Watch for breezy winds and low relative humidity, which
is in effect from Wednesday afternoon through Wednesday evening.

* WINDS...10-20 mph gusting as high as 25-30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 15-30 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Mid to upper 90s.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread quickly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.

alerts.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued March 10 at 2:44PM CDT until March 11 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
alerts.description:
...ELEVATED TO CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER RISK EXPECTED ON WEDNESDAY...

.A precipitous drop off in relative humidity (RH) values are
expected to take place Wednesday afternoon following the passage
of a dryline. The combination of low RH values ranging between
15-30%, an ongoing drought ranging from D2 (Severe Drought) to D4
(Exceptional Drought), and breezy northwest winds will result in
elevated to critical fire weather risk on Wednesday across all of
Deep South Texas, excluding the island.

The National Weather Service in Brownsville has issued a Fire
Weather Watch for breezy winds and low relative humidity, which
is in effect from Wednesday afternoon through Wednesday evening.

* WINDS...10-20 mph gusting as high as 25-30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 15-30 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Mid to upper 90s.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread quickly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.

alerts.headline: Flood Advisory issued March 10 at 9:14PM CDT until March 11 at 12:15AM CDT by NWS Fort Worth TX
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Urban and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Portions of central and north central Texas, including the
following counties, in central Texas, Comanche. In north central
Texas, Erath, Hood, Palo Pinto, Parker and Somervell.

* WHEN...Until 1215 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to thunderstorms. This
will likely cause urban and small stream flooding. Low lying
and/or poor drainage areas will experience minor flooding in
the advisory area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Weatherford, Stephenville, Mineral Wells, Azle, Granbury,
Comanche, Dublin, Briar, Pecan Plantation, Willow Park, Reno,
Aledo, Springtown, Glen Rose, Brock, Hudson Oaks, Western
Lake, Annetta, Poolville and Gustine.

alerts.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued March 10 at 2:44PM CDT until March 11 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
alerts.description:
...ELEVATED TO CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER RISK EXPECTED ON WEDNESDAY...

.A precipitous drop off in relative humidity (RH) values are
expected to take place Wednesday afternoon following the passage
of a dryline. The combination of low RH values ranging between
15-30%, an ongoing drought ranging from D2 (Severe Drought) to D4
(Exceptional Drought), and breezy northwest winds will result in
elevated to critical fire weather risk on Wednesday across all of
Deep South Texas, excluding the island.

The National Weather Service in Brownsville has issued a Fire
Weather Watch for breezy winds and low relative humidity, which
is in effect from Wednesday afternoon through Wednesday evening.

* WINDS...10-20 mph gusting as high as 25-30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 15-30 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Mid to upper 90s.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread quickly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
